notes: One-character play (docs/ONE_CHARACTER_PLAN.md Revision 3). Every number the owner may tune by playing lives here. Per-difficulty values are keyed relaxed (Easy) / normal / hard. Read through SoloCfg.

opening._doc: Task 61A, read by SoloOpening and SoloTeach. Each moment is said once, from a real system: the landlord's note (the real first rent), the neighbour's visit (StoryVisits), a Help wanted card near home (an opening at the nearest business that has staff), and one first-week moment per background (day = days after the start; kinds: loan = the real loan's payment and due day, probation = a check-in in the calendar, contact = the creation contact, lead = a real job lead). teach = the first-time lines.

landlord.line: A note under the door from {who}, the landlord: "Rent's due {due}. {amount} coins."
landlord.line_paid: A note under the door from {who}, the landlord: "Rent's paid till {due}. {amount} coins a week after that."

neighbour.line: {who} from next door knocks to say hello.

neighbour_again.line: {who} from next door drops by again. "A word about the landlord: pay on the day. The locks get changed fast round here."

college_dropout.line: A letter from the student loan office: {pay} coins a week, the first on {due}.

follow.line: The first student loan payment went out: {pay} coins.

in_debt.line: The loan shop rings: {pay} coins a week, the first on {due}. "Don't make us come round."

follow.line: The loan shop rings again, after dark. "{pay} on {due}. We know where the studio is."

ex_con.line: A letter from the probation office: check in at the police station on {when}.
ex_con.done: You check in at the front desk. The officer stamps your card.
ex_con.over: Your last check-in. The officer signs you off: probation is over.
ex_con.warning: A letter from the probation office: you missed your check-in. Report on {when}, or it goes to court.
ex_con.missed: A letter from the probation office: you missed another check-in, and they have told the police.

street_kid.line: {who} texts: "Heard you got a place. Come find me in the Kiln Quarter."
street_kid.line_no_phone: {who} catches you in the street: "Heard you got a place. Come find me in the Kiln Quarter."

follow.line: {who} turns up at your door. "You never came by. Thought I'd come to you."

retail_worker.line: {who}, who used to work the till with you, says the {place} is after a cashier.

trade_apprentice.line: {who} from next door has a gate that sticks, and says the market is after an odd-jobber.

follow.ask: Your old boss rings: a big job at the works yard on {when}, and they need you for the day. Unpaid. "You owe me, and you want that reference."
follow.kept: Your old boss nods at the gate. "Good. The reference stands."
follow.lost: Your old boss won't vouch for you now.

delivery_driver.line: {who} says the depot at the works yard is taking on pickers and packers this week.

kitchen_hand.line: {who} from the café kitchen says they're a dishwasher short.

care_worker.line: {who} says the school needs teaching aides, and that care work counts.

hunger.line: Your stomach growls. {coins} coins and nothing in the cupboard.

no_bed.line: No bed yet. The floor it is.

first_bill.line: The first bill. It pays itself on the day it's due, if the coins are there.

shelter.cause: The council runs a shelter because people lose their homes; it gives you a bed, not a meal.

ladder.label: The street
ladder.cause: Nobody owns the bench, so nobody charges for it; nobody keeps it safe either.

ladder.label: Night shelter
ladder.cause: The council pays for a few beds; it cannot pay for more nights.

ladder.label: Bedsit at Elm Court
ladder.cause: A room in somebody else's house is cheap because you share everything.

ladder.label: Council flat at Elm Court
ladder.cause: The council lets flats below market to people with little income, so you apply and you wait.

ladder.label: Starter Studio
ladder.cause: A private landlord lets the studio at the going rate.

ladder.label: Better flat (Cedar Court)
ladder.cause: Market rent of a 10,000 coin property.

ladder.label: Family house (Maple Row)
ladder.cause: A 15,000 to 21,000 coin property with a garden and a quiet street.

grey._doc: Task 61c, read by SoloGrey: outside the rough districts someone the pawn knows (friendship >= min_friendship) offers grey money once the pawn is in trouble (broke_coins, no job, a late bill). caught = the chance it comes back 2-5 days later as a fine and a petty record.

offers.title: Cash in hand
offers.line: {who} has a van and a flat to clear. "Four hours, {pay} cash, nobody needs to know."
offers.caught_line: A letter from the tax office: undeclared cash work. A fine of {fine} coins.

offers.title: Fell off a truck
offers.line: {who} has a box of trainers that "fell off a truck". "Sell them on and keep {pay}. Easy."
offers.away: Selling trainers out of a box
offers.caught_line: The police traced the trainers back to you: handling stolen goods. A fine of {fine} coins.
